answers.M8-S1: The author does an experiment taking mason bees far from their nest to see if they can find their way home, and some of them do.
answers.M8-S2: To show the trip got harder. The wind made it tough for the author to carry the bees and get home, so he didn't think it would work.
answers.M8-S3: It suggests Aglaé had been out collecting while she waited, so the bees came back loaded and weren't even tired from the trip.
answers.M8-S4: So Aglaé could tell which bees were the ones he took away when they came back to the nest.
answers.M8-S5: At first he doubts the bees will make it home, but when Aglaé says two arrived he is surprised and excited that it worked.
answers.M8-S6: In time order, telling the steps of the experiment from catching the bees to finding out the results.
answers.M8-S7: To show how fast the bees flew home, two and a half miles in under 45 minutes, even with stopping on the way.
answers.M8-S8: To show how hard the job was, because the bees stung him so many times that half of them got hurt.
answers.M8-S9: That the author couldn't see where they went, so he didn't know which way they flew or if they got home.
